newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Inquiry launched into Colombian cement industry.
newsitem.headline: Inquiry launched into Colombian cement industry.

text.p: Colombia's trade and industry superintendency said Wednesday it had launched an official investigation into allegations of unfair trading practices in the country's cement industry.

The inquiry will focus on the activities of the Colombian Cement Producers Institute (ICPC) and cement manufacturers Cemento Argos, Paz del Rio, both part of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno industrial conglomerate, Cementos Diamante, owned by the world's fourth largest manufacturer Cemex of Mexico, and Cementos Boyacau, owned by Switzerland's Holderbank .
"The investigation will cover 98 percent of the country's gray cement manufacturers who annually produce six million tonnes," the superintendency's statement said.

"In the case of the ICPC, we found that producers were exchanging information on prices and sales of gray cement ... we will check to see if this procedure distorted the rules of free competition in this market," it added.

The superintendency said there were also indications that the cement producers had cut a deal to "divide up the market geographically, a practice expressly forbidden." This alleged agreement led to limited supplies, minimal choice and skyrocketing prices in regional markets, the superintendency said.
The cement companies were unavailable for immediate comment on the launch of the investigation.
